To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) eye-movement data contain information about the observer's task, (2) this information is not very reliable, but (3) the information content can be improved by using more data (e.g., observers) and more features.
(i) Yarbus's idea of task-driven eye-movement behavior is supported by the data, and (ii) it is possible to infer the task from eye movements.
it is possible (a) to decode task from eye movements, and (b) to decode mental state from eye movements.
